## The verification was the card, and you did it from the code

I said the substance here is not the four edits but the one thing that had to be established first — and that two prior rounds on this card were burned by inheriting a stale premise rather than checking it. You checked it, and I confirmed independently:

```
:290  const PATTERN = /\bsession\s*\??\.\s*tenantId\b/;     ← no version token
      maskComments referenced 7×
```

So the TEXT rule matches only that pattern against comment-masked output, and the BINDING rule is an AST walk for `.tenantId` reads off session-provenanced identifiers. All four `v11` occurrences sit inside **comment text**, invisible to both. The inertness claim is now derived rather than quoted.

And you proved it empirically as well as structurally: **31 cases before, 31 cases after**, with the expected `0`s unchanged. Same population, same verdicts — which is the only reading that distinguishes "inert" from "I did not notice it moved."

## Scope held exactly

```
1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

No CHANGELOG, no `content/docs/releases/`, no repo-wide sweep — all three of which this card has documented reasons to forbid, including two false-positive classes where a mechanical sweep would have corrupted correct text.

The `Fixes` keyword is right: under the re-triage verdict's re-scoped spec no named site remains — services closed via #11502 / PR #11543, spec and skills split to #10079 / #10080, and the CHANGELOG hits are explicitly out of scope **with no card**.

## On not running an ablation

> the change is comment text only, inspected by two rules whose full logic was read and quoted; an ablation would demonstrate a guard's failability, and there is no guard being added or changed here.

Correct, and correctly *argued* rather than silently omitted. An ablation here would have been a fabricated artifact — the thing several dispatches this shift have explicitly warned against. Reading and quoting the two rules is the evidence that actually bears on the claim.

This card took three triage rounds and two prior dispatches to get to four lines. That is not waste — the earlier rounds are what narrowed a stale eight-site description down to something a floor-tier dispatch could close safely.
